title: What the federal retail rules for scheduled listed chemical products reach, and their effect on State law
subtopic: Coverage, definitions and effect on State law
rule_summary: 21 CFR part 1314 specifies the requirements for retail sales of scheduled listed chemical products to individuals for personal use (1314.01). It applies to regulated sellers of scheduled listed chemical products sold at retail for personal use through face-to-face sales at stores or mobile retail vendors, and to regulated persons who engage in a transaction with a non-regulated person and ship the products by the U.S. Postal Service or by private or common carriers; the requirements of subpart A apply to all regulated persons subject to the part, those of subpart B to regulated sellers as defined in 21 CFR 1300.02, and those of subpart C to regulated persons who ship the products to the customer by the U.S. Postal Service or by private or common carriers (1314.02). A mail-order sale is a retail sale of scheduled listed chemical products for personal use where a regulated person uses or attempts to use the U.S. Postal Service or any private or commercial carrier to deliver the product to the customer, and includes purchase orders submitted by phone, mail, fax, Internet, or any method other than a face-to-face transaction (1314.03). Under 21 CFR 1300.02, a scheduled listed chemical product is a product that contains ephedrine, pseudoephedrine, or phenylpropanolamine (including their salts, optical isomers, and salts of optical isomers) and may be marketed or distributed lawfully in the United States under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act as a nonprescription drug, and the term does not include any product that is a controlled substance under part 1308; a regulated seller is a retail distributor (including a pharmacy or a mobile retail vendor), except that the term does not include an employee or agent of the distributor; a retail distributor is a grocery store, general merchandise store, drug store, or other entity or person whose activities as a distributor relating to drug products containing ephedrine, pseudoephedrine, or phenylpropanolamine are limited almost exclusively to sales for personal use, both in number of sales and volume of sales, either directly to walk-in customers or in face-to-face transactions by direct sales; and a mobile retail vendor is a person or entity that makes sales at retail from a stand that is intended to be temporary or is capable of being moved from one location to another. Under 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(F), the retail-transaction requirements of 830(e)(1)(A) do not apply to the sale at retail of a scheduled listed chemical product if a report on the sales transaction is required to be submitted under 830(b)(3). Under 21 CFR 1314.10, nothing in part 1314 preempts State law on the same subject matter unless there is a positive conflict between the part and a State law so that the two cannot consistently stand together.
exam_relevance: Tests who and what the federal retail rules reach - a pharmacy is a regulated seller and its employees and agents are not - how face-to-face and shipped sales are divided between subparts B and C, and that part 1314 leaves consistent State law in place.

exceptions: Under 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(F), the retail-transaction requirements of 830(e)(1)(A) do not apply to a retail sale for which a report on the sales transaction is required under 830(b)(3); such sales are subject to 830(e)(2).
common_confusions: An employee or agent of a retail distributor is not a regulated seller; the duties of subpart B fall on the distributor.
A scheduled listed chemical product is a product that may lawfully be marketed as a nonprescription drug; a product that is a controlled substance under part 1308 is not one.
Part 1314 does not preempt State law on the same subject matter unless the two cannot consistently stand together.
